articles.title: FDA Accepts Priority Review For Takeda’s Zasocitinib In Plaque Psoriasis

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence Analysis Of Social Media Uncovers Undocumented Ozempic Side Effects
articles.summary: Researchers utilized artificial intelligence to analyze over 400,000 Reddit posts, successfully identifying previously undocumented side effects associated with the blockbuster weight-loss and diabetes drug Ozempic. This matters because patient-reported digital data offers real-world safety insights that often circumvent traditional clinical trial timelines and reporting mechanisms. For self-funded employers and pharmacy benefits managers, the emergence of novel side effects could shift utilization patterns, alter long-term adherence, and ultimately impact overall plan expenditures regarding GLP-1 therapies.

articles.title: Evaluating 2026 Financial Models: Annual Prepay Versus Month-to-Month GLP-1 Coverage Strategies
articles.summary: This analysis explores the financial viability of pre-paying annually for GLP-1 medications compared to traditional month-to-month purchasing models heading into 2026. As employer-sponsored self-funded plans grapple with soaring specialty drug costs, understanding these alternative payment structures is critical for accurate budgeting and cost containment. For organizations partnering with a pharmacy benefits manager, determining the optimal financial structure helps mitigate unpredictable pharmacy spend while balancing comprehensive employee access to high-demand weight-loss therapies.

articles.title: National Comprehensive Cancer Network Survey Reveals Ongoing Cancer Drug Shortages Impacting US Medical Centers
articles.summary: A recent National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) survey highlights persistent shortages of critical cancer drugs across United States treatment centers, forcing healthcare providers to alter established care protocols. This matters because supply chain instability for complex oncology therapies drives up treatment costs, delays vital patient care, and increases financial toxicity for employers managing self-funded health plans. Key business implications include the urgent need for pharmacy benefits strategies that proactively identify alternative therapeutic pathways, manage specialty drug utilization, and protect plan members from disruptions in high-cost oncology care.
